title: Story 01: New Feature Request — Full Lifecycle
pmResponse:
# Action Plan: "Add search functionality to the issue list"

## Step 0 — Scope Analysis (Reasoning Before Commands)

**Request:** "Add search functionality to the issue list"

**Scope determination:** Applying the scope heuristic from the skill — is this about data/logic or about presentation/UI? "Search functionality" on "the issue list" is a **data/backend layer** feature. The issue list is data; search is a data-query capability. The request does NOT use words like "screen", "page", or "UI", so I must NOT add a second track for the Webapp team. This is a **single Library sub-team deliverable**.

**Phase flow:** Feature → Plan → Dev → Validate → Release (4 phases, 4 tasks).

**Agents:**
- Plan → `library-architect` (architecture/API design needed for search)
- Dev → `library-developer`
- Validate → `library-validator`
- Release → `library-releaser`

**Hierarchy decision:** One deliverable with 4 phase tasks → a `feature` parent over 4 `task` children. No Epic/Initiative needed (only one deliverable). No verification child (the status loop completes the parent).

---

## Step 1 — Create the parent Feature issue

```
agt create "Add search functionality to the issue list" \
  --tags feature \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo
```

**Reasoning:** This is the single deliverable. It's a new user-facing capability → `feature` tag. Assigned to me (PM) as the parent. Left at `todo` per Rule 2 — the status loop will auto-promote it to `in-progress` when a worker starts the first child, preventing the work loop from re-waking me every cycle.

**Assume this returns issue ID `P`.**

---

## Step 2 — Create the four phase tasks as children

### Phase 1 — Plan

```
agt create "Plan search functionality for issue list" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee library-architect \
  --status todo \
  --parentId P
```

**Reasoning:** Search functionality needs architecture/API design (what query interface to expose, how to index/filter, what fields are searchable). This is not a trivial addition, so planning goes to the `library-architect` (not the developer). One task per phase — never collapsed.

**Assume this returns issue ID `T1`.**

### Phase 2 — Development

```
agt create "Implement search functionality for issue list" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee library-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId P
```

**Reasoning:** Implementation goes to the `library-developer` (never a validator). This is the dev phase.

**Assume this returns issue ID `T2`.**

### Phase 3 — Validation

```
agt create "Validate search functionality for issue list" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee library-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId P
```

**Reasoning:** Validation is ALWAYS a separate task assigned to the team's validator — the developer who built it never validates their own work.

**Assume this returns issue ID `T3`.**

### Phase 4 — Release

```
agt create "Release search functionality for issue list" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee library-releaser \
  --status todo \
  --parentId P
```

**Reasoning:** Release phase — runs tests, generates docs, builds, publishes. The releaser is a gate; if tests fail, release stops.

**Assume this returns issue ID `T4`.**

---

## Step 3 — Create blockages to chain the phases sequentially

```
agt blockages add T2 --by T1
agt blockages add T3 --by T2
agt blockages add T4 --by T3
```

**Reasoning:** The phase chain must flow sequentially: Dev can't start until Plan is done; Validate can't start until Dev is done; Release can't start until Validate is done. When each task is marked `done`, the system **auto-resolves** the blockage it was causing, which unblocks the next task. I never run `agt blockages resolve` in the work loop — the auto-clear is the engine.

---

## Step 4 — Add a comment to the parent for context

```
agt comments add P --content "Feature: add search to the issue list. Library sub-team deliverable. Phase chain: Plan (library-architect) → Dev (library-developer) → Validate (library-validator) → Release (library-releaser). Parent left at todo — status loop auto-promotes when first child starts and completes parent when all children are done."
```

**Reasoning:** Document the plan so the work is traceable. This records the scope decision (Library-only, data-layer feature) and the phase assignments.

---

## Complete Issue Hierarchy

```
P  [feature] "Add search functionality to the issue list"
   assignee: project-manager | status: todo
   │
   ├── T1  [task] "Plan search functionality for issue list"
   │        assignee: library-architect | status: todo
   │        (unblocked — work loop will pick this up first)
   │
   ├── T2  [task] "Implement search functionality for issue list"
   │        assignee: library-developer | status: todo
   │        blocked by: T1
   │
   ├── T3  [task] "Validate search functionality for issue list"
   │        assignee: library-validator | status: todo
   │        blocked by: T2
   │
   └── T4  [task] "Release search functionality for issue list"
            assignee: library-releaser | status: todo
            blocked by: T3
```

**Blockage chain:** `T1 → T2 → T3 → T4` (each blocks the next)

---

## What Happens Next (No PM Action Required)

1. **Work loop picks up T1** (it's `todo`, assigned to `library-architect`, no open blockages) → hands it to the architect → architect sets it `in-progress`.
2. **Status loop auto-promotes P** from `todo` → `in-progress` (because a child started).
3. Architect completes T1 (sets `done` + comment) → blockage on T2 **auto-clears** → work loop picks up T2 → hands to `library-developer`.
4. Developer completes T2 → blockage on T3 auto-clears → `library-validator` gets T3.
5. Validator completes T3 → blockage on T4 auto-clears → `library-releaser` gets T4.
6. Releaser completes T4 → all children of P are `done`.
7. **Status loop finds P** `in-progress` with all children `done` → P has **no parent** (top-level deliverable) → marks P `closed` AND closes all descendants (T1–T4). Work fully delivered and cleared from the tracker.

---

## Summary of Every Command (in execution order)

| # | Command | Purpose |
|---|---------|---------|
| 1 | `agt create "Add search functionality to the issue list" --tags feature --assignee project-manager --status todo` | Create parent deliverable |
| 2 | `agt create "Plan search functionality for issue list" --tags task --assignee library-architect --status todo --parentId P` | Phase 1 task |
| 3 | `agt create "Implement search functionality for issue list" --tags task --assignee library-developer --status todo --parentId P` | Phase 2 task |
| 4 | `agt create "Validate search functionality for issue list" --tags task --assignee library-validator --status todo --parentId P` | Phase 3 task |
| 5 | `agt create "Release search functionality for issue list" --tags task --assignee library-releaser --status todo --parentId P` | Phase 4 task |
| 6 | `agt blockages add T2 --by T1` | Chain: Plan → Dev |
| 7 | `agt blockages add T3 --by T2` | Chain: Dev → Validate |
| 8 | `agt blockages add T4 --by T3` | Chain: Validate → Release |
| 9 | `agt comments add P --content "Feature: add search to the issue list..."` | Document scope & plan |

**Total:** 1 parent + 4 tasks + 3 blockages + 1 comment = 9 commands. No gate tracker needed (single-team, no cross-team provider/consumer relationship). No verification child (status loop completes the parent). Parent stays at `todo` — PM steps back.
feedback: Excellent response. Correct single-team scope determination (Library-only, no Webapp track). Feature parent over 4 phase tasks with no single-child anti-pattern. Phase-to-agent mapping exactly right (architect/developer/validator/releaser). Sequential blockage chain T1→T2→T3→T4 with auto-resolve understanding. Parent correctly left at todo (never flipped to in-progress), no verification/sync child created, no gate tracker (single-team, no review gate). Status-loop completion behavior (top-level parent closed + children closed) accurately described. Minor cosmetic differences in task titles (\"Plan\" vs \"Design\") are immaterial.
